chapter.subject: Science
chapter.chapter: Chapter 7 — Work, Energy, and Simple Machines

excerpts:
[INJSO 2009 — question paper]
1. Which one of the following expressions has the same units as power?
a) Force x distance
b) Work x time
¢) Force x acceleration
d) Force x velocity

[INJSO 2010 — question paper]
46. A trolley runs from point P to Q along a track, as shown in the figure. At point Q,
its potential energy is 50 kJ less than at point P. At point P, the trolley has kinetic energy
5 kJ. Between P and Q, the work done against friction is 10 kJ. What is the kinetic energy
at point Q?
a) 35 kJ b) 45 kJ c) 55 kJ d) 65 kJ

[INJSO 2012 — question paper]
1. A load is to be moved using a wheelbarrow. The total mass of the load and wheelbarrow is 60 kg.
The magnitude of gravitational acceleration is 10 ms 2 .
What is the work done if the handle is raised by 50 cm?
a) 35.0 J
b) 17.5 J
c) 175 J
d) 350 J

[INJSO 2012 — question paper]
45. The diagram shows a lift system in which the elevator (mass m 1 ) is partly counterbalanced by a
heavy weight (mass m 2 ).
At what rate does the motor provide energy to the system when the elevator is rising at a steady
speed v ? (g = acceleration of free fall) (consider the pulley as frictionless at the pivot)
a) (m 1 + m 2 )gv
b) ½ (m 1 + m 2 )gv
c) (m 1 m 2 )gv /(m 1 + m 2 )
d) (m 1 – m 2 )gv

items.stem: What is the scientific definition of work done by a constant force on an object?

If an object is moved horizontally with a force of 15 N over a distance of 4 m, what is the work done?
When is work done by a force on an object considered negative?

What is the energy stored in a deformed object due to its shape called?

Based on the potential energy-displacement graph in Fig. 7.39, what is the velocity of the ball at point P?
If the gravitational attraction on the Moon is one-sixth of that on Earth, how far will a ball travel on the Moon if it is thrown with the same upward velocity as on Earth?
What is the term for the capacity of an object to do work?
Which of the following is an example of a simple machine that changes the direction of the force applied?
A 2 kg object is lifted vertically to a height of 5 m. What is the potential energy gained by the object? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
A water mill converts potential energy into kinetic energy. Which of the following statements best explains this conversion?

Based on the experiment described, what is the condition for the beam to balance?

A student pushes a box up a frictionless ramp. The box is lifted to a height of 1.5 m. The ramp is 3 m long. What is the mechanical advantage of the ramp?
Which of the following is an example of potential energy due to the relative position of objects in a system?
If a force of 10 N is applied to move an object 5 m in the direction of the force, what is the work done?
A force of 20 N is applied to move an object 3 m in the direction of the force. What is the work done?
A car of mass 1000 kg starts from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/h in 10 seconds. What is the power of the engine required to achieve this start?
What is the unit of potential energy?
What is the unit of potential energy?
What is the SI unit of work?
A weightlifter lifts a 75 kg mass by 2 m in 5 seconds. What is the power required for this task?
When you pedal a bicycle on a flat road, your muscles supply energy. In what forms does this muscular energy appear as you ride?
A ball of mass 5 kg is lifted to a height of 10 m above the ground. What is the gravitational potential energy of the ball? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
